questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A steel wire of diameter $0.5mm$ and Young's modulus $2 \times {10}^{11}N{m}^{- 2}$ carries a load of mass M. The length of the wire with the load is 1.0 m. A vernier scale with 10 divisions is attached to the end of this wire. Next to the steel wire is a reference wire to which a main scale, of least count 1.0 mm, is attached. The 10 divisions of the vernier scale correspond to 9 divisions of the main scale. Initially, the zero of vernier scale coincides with the zero of main scale. If the load on the steel wire is increased by $1.2kg$ , the vernier scale division which coincides with a main scale division is __________. Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 1}and\pi = 3.2 .$
questions.solution:
$d = 0.5mm$
$Y = 2 \times {10}^{11}$
$l = 1m$
$∆ l = \dfrac{Fl}{Ay} = \dfrac{mgl}{\dfrac{\pi{d}^{2}}{4}y} = \dfrac{1.2 \times 10 \times 1}{\dfrac{\pi}{4} \times {\left(5 \times {10}^{- 4}\right)}^{2} \times 2 \times {10}^{11}}$
$∆ l = \dfrac{1.2 \times 10}{\dfrac{3.2}{4} \times 25 \times {10}^{- 8} \times 2 \times {10}^{11}}$
$= \dfrac{12}{1.6 \times 25 \times {10}^{3}} = \dfrac{12}{40 \times {10}^{3}} = 0.03mm$
So 3rd division of vernier scale will coincicle with main scale

questions.q: In plotting stress versus strain curves for two materials $P$ and $Q$ , a student by mistake puts strain on the $y$ -axis and stress on the $x$ - axis as shown in the figure. Then the correct statement(s) is(are)
options: The Young's modulus of  $P$  is more than that of  $Q$
questions.solution:
Slope of this graph represents the reciprocal of Young's modulus.
Since slope of $P >$ slope of Q
Hence Y of $P < Y$ of Q

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One end of a horizontal thick copper wire of length $2L$and radius $2R$ is welded to an end of another horizontal thin copper wire of length$L$ and radius$R$. When the arrangement stretched by applying forces at two ends, the ratio of the elongation in the thin wire to that in the thick wire is
questions.solution:
As the two rods are in series, the force at the connecting surface will be same.

${F}_{1} = {F}_{2}$

$⇒ Y \times \dfrac{∆ {l}_{1}}{{l}_{1}} \times {A}_{1} = Y \times \dfrac{∆ {l}_{2}}{{l}_{2}} \times {A}_{2}$

Where $Y$ is Young's modulus, $∆ {l}_{1} and ∆ {l}_{2}$ is increase in length, ${l}_{1} and {l}_{2}$ are lengths, ${A}_{1} and {A}_{2}$ are areas, $2R and R$ are radii of thick and thin wires respectively.

$\left[\text{∵ F} = \text{Y} \times \text{strain} \times \text{Area}\right]$

$⇒ \dfrac{∆ {l}_{1}}{{l}_{1}} \times {A}_{1} = \dfrac{∆ {l}_{2}}{{l}_{2}} \times {A}_{2}$

Here, ${A}_{1} = \pi{\left(2R\right)}^{2}, {l}_{1} = 2L$

${A}_{2} = {\pi R}^{2}, {l}_{2} = L$
$⇒ \dfrac{∆ {l}_{1}}{2L} \times \pi{\left(2R\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{∆ {l}_{2}}{L} \times {\pi R}^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{∆ {l}_{2}}{∆ {l}_{1}} = 2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A $0.1 \mathrm{~kg}$ mass is suspended from a wire of negligible mass. The length of the wire is $1 \mathrm{~m}$ and its cross-sectional area is $4.9 \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{~m}^2$. If the mass is pulled a little in the vertically downward direction and released, it performs simple harmonic motion of angular frequency $140 \mathrm{rad} \mathrm{s}^{-1}$. If the Young's modulus of the material of the wire is $n \times 10^9 \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$, the value of $n$ is
questions.solution:
$\omega=\sqrt{\frac{K}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{Y A}{l m}}=\sqrt{\frac{\left(n \times 10^9\right)\left(4.9 \times 10^{-7}\right)}{1 \times 0.1}}$
Putting, $\omega=140 \operatorname{rad} \mathrms^{-1}$ in above equation we get,

n=4

$\therefore$ Answer is 4 .
